svg.text: The model: a protein becomes a few pocket vectors, a ligand becomes one, and binding is a dot product
Trained end to end, contrastively, on dataset_v2. At screening time each side is encoded once; no per-pair docking or simulation.
score(protein, ligand) = max over its 8 anchors of cos(aₖ, ℓ) / τ
a protein binds a ligand if ANY of its pockets matches; τ is learned
each true pair (diagonal) must outscore every
other protein and every other ligand
same target, same ligand, or Tanimoto ≥ 0.8
One row per target per batch
pocket BCE on the logit (box 5): keeps the regions on real pockets
Tanimoto pull, weight 0.05: ligands at Tanimoto T ≥ 0.5 asked for cos ≥ T
encode every protein once and every ligand once and store the vectors; a screen is then
one matrix of dot products between them, instead of one docking or simulation run per
protein-ligand pair. The protein side needs no ligand and no known binding site:
the pocket logit chooses where to look (boxes 5-6).
